evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login succeeded despite a nonce semantic mismatch (IdP omitted nonce in id_token while nonce was sent), enabling potential replay/login CSRF against the brokered SSO flow.

sequence_description: Revocation freshness: obtain an API-bound access token (JWT by specifying resource), introspect it (should be active), revoke it, then introspect again (should be inactive/rejected). Include a second identity as a control.
description: [LLM-Judge] Freshly obtained access tokens introspect as inactive (active=false) even before any revocation, suggesting either broken introspection usage/config or tokens being treated as invalid immediately.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Freshly obtained access tokens introspect as inactive (active=false) even before any revocation, suggesting either broken introspection usage/config or tokens being treated as invalid immediately.

sequence_description: I4 attack: Unicode normalization collision in upstream subject/name (NFC vs NFD) via controllable IdP claims; ensure distinct upstream principals do not collapse to one downstream identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML logins for two distinct upstream principals (NFC vs NFD) created distinct downstream users, but both were assigned the same display_name as an existing local user, which could enable UI/account confusion if display_name is treated as an identifier anywhere.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML logins for two distinct upstream principals (NFC vs NFD) created distinct downstream users, but both were assigned the same display_name as an existing local user, which could enable UI/account confusion if display_name is treated as an identifier anywhere.

sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user then SAML SSO login with same email but different upstream principal (NameID/sub). Verify they do NOT collapse into one identity when email is verified (tests over-aggressive email-based linking).
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-protocol account linking occurred: SAML SSO login (different upstream principal) was merged into the existing local password user solely based on the same verified email, enabling potential account takeover if an attacker controls an IdP asserting that email.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-protocol account linking occurred: SAML SSO login (different upstream principal) was merged into the existing local password user solely based on the same verified email, enabling potential account takeover if an attacker controls an IdP asserting that email.
